text:
aj: Heads up — over the last 2 hours I see ~100 reserved GPUs stuck in a 'reserved' state but not actually allocated, pods pending with AttachVolume/AttachBlock errors. Appears concentrated in us-west2 racks R3-R5. Anyone seen this pattern?
maria: Yep, saw spikes on the reclaim dashboard. Looks like reservation objects aren't being cleared when a node reports Ready->NotReady quickly. kubelet logs show: `E attachdetacher: Timeout waiting for attach` and then reservation controller never reclaims.
leo: That rings a bell — 1.26.3 had an attach/detach edge where the reservation finalizer isn't removed on rapid network flaps. Could be our kubelet build.
ops-jen: Can we verify whether pods are actually orphaned vs. still bound? Quick `kubectl get pods -o wide | grep Pending` shows a bunch with `nodeSelector: reserved=true` and `Status: Pending`.
aj: Pasted sample: ```kubectl describe pod gpu-train-xyz```
Containers: Waiting
  Reason: AttachVolumeTimeout
Events:
  3m   Warning  FailedAttachVolume  attach-detacher  timeout waiting for volume attach for volume "gpu-shelf-claim"
```
maria: Fleet telemetry: ~120 GPUs impacted, across 3 racks, mostly us-west2a/b. That’s ~1.5% of our pool. Cost-wise if they stay stranded for 12h it's ~ $6k in effective wasted reserved capacity (est).
leo: Short-term mitigation: run a targeted descheduler job to evict pods with the `reserved-lock=stale` annotation so the reservation controller can reclaim. I can draft a job that filters by label + node affinity to avoid noisy evictions.
ops-jen: Agreed. Could also temporarily relax the scheduler's `preferReservedScore` so new workloads don't aggressively pin to these 'ghost' reservations — reduces queueing. But we should be careful about impacting latency-critical routes.
aj: Who owns the descheduler run? Also want an alert to escalate if reclamation rate < 10 GPUs/hour.
ops-jen: I'll own the descheduler cron for the next 6 hours. Plan: 1) one-off descheduler run for the 3 racks 2) enable an automated 30m cron if reclaim rate stays low 3) patch rollout plan for kubelet.
leo: For medium-term, we should implement a scheduler-side "reclaimer" that can forcibly clear a reservation after X minutes of attach failures and mark the node as suspect. Calling it `pin_shed` internally so we can A/B test. It would avoid heavy eviction churn since it only operates on reservation metadata.
maria: Agree on reclaimer. Also we should add a cost metric to the alert — `stranded_gpu_cost_last_6h` so finance can see day-over-day.
scheduling-bot: Canary patch to kubelet (attach/detach timeout handling) landed in canary cluster at 1719003000 — rolling to us-west2a as a pilot. Will report back. :robot_face:
deploy-bot: Alert created: `gpu.reservation.stalled` with severity P2, paging on owner group `eng-platform-ops`. Link: https://monitoring/redwood/alerts/8341
aj: OK then short term actions: ops-jen run descheduler now (confirmed), scheduling-bot monitor canary, leo prototype `pin_shed` reclaimer. I'll update the incident channel once we see reclaim progress. :thumbsup:
ops-jen: Running descheduler now — filter: `app=gpu-worker, reserved-lock=stale, topology.kubernetes.io/zone=us-west2a,us-west2b` — starting with a small batch (10 pods) to watch eviction ripple.
maria: Current reclaim delta: +8 GPUs reclaimed in 10m after first batch. If that keeps, we can limit broader descheduler.
leo: I'll sketch the pin_shed design and post a short PR for review later today.
aj: Thanks all. If reclaim stalls, we'll escalate to rolling kubelet rollback.
